items.title: Changing item 99's price calls the CatalogItemPriceChange webhook once with the id, new price and old price
covers: Steps to Reproduce 1-4
Expected: destination receives one webhook call with the item's id, new price and old price
Expected: the webhooks client lists it among the received messages
Acceptance Criteria
items.reason: This is the bug itself: the Steps to Reproduce, run on the test stack, must end with exactly one received message for the price change. The message must hold the item id, the new price and the old price. The defect lives between services (Catalog API publishes, the event bus delivers, the Webhooks API handler sends, the webhooks client receives). Only the running stack exercises that chain, so the case is `e2e`, following the ticket's own steps.

items.title: The price-change handler sends WebhookData of type CatalogItemPriceChange carrying ProductId, NewPrice and OldPrice to the CatalogItemPriceChange subscriptions
covers: Expected: webhook call with the event CatalogItemPriceChange
Expected: the item's id, its new price and its old price
Code map: ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEventHandler
items.reason: The ticket requires the call to carry the event `CatalogItemPriceChange`. The webhooks client drops `Type` when it stores a message, so the e2e case cannot observe the event name. This unit case pins it, and also pins that the handler sends to the price-change subscriptions and not to another type's. It lives in `tests/Application.UnitTests`, which already references `Webhooks.API`, with NSubstitute substitutes and no running services.

items.title: An update of item 99 that keeps its price calls no webhook
covers: Expected: a price update that does not change the price calls nothing
items.reason: The ticket says a price update that leaves the price unchanged calls nothing. This is the boundary of "price changed": new price equal to old price. If it broke, every catalog edit would notify subscribers with a fake price change. Whether an event is published is decided in the Catalog API, and the absence of a call is only observable at the destination. So the case runs on the test stack, with the same registration as TC-BUG-53-01.

items.title: A price change calls no OrderPaid or OrderShipped webhook
covers: Expected: webhooks registered for OrderPaid and OrderShipped behave exactly as today
Expected: the destination receives one webhook call for the price change
items.reason: The fix must route the price change only to `CatalogItemPriceChange` registrations. Today a price change calls no `OrderPaid` or `OrderShipped` webhook, and that must stay true. If the new handler fetched every subscription, or the wrong type, order webhooks would receive catalog messages. Distinct tokens per event make the receiver of each call visible on the webhooks client's page. Delivery is only observable on the running stack, so the case runs on the `e2e` layer.

items.title: The OrderPaid handler still sends WebhookData of type OrderPaid to the OrderPaid subscriptions
covers: Expected: webhooks registered for OrderPaid behave exactly as today
items.reason: The ticket requires `OrderPaid` webhooks to behave exactly as today, and the fix copied the OrderPaid handler's pattern into a sibling handler. This case pins the OrderPaid handler's routing (subscriptions of type `OrderPaid`, `WebhookData.Type` `OrderPaid`, the event as payload) so a shared refactor cannot change it. A real paid order cannot be produced cheaply on the stack, so the routing is checked in process. It lives in `tests/Application.UnitTests` with NSubstitute substitutes.

items.title: The OrderShipped handler still sends WebhookData of type OrderShipped to the OrderShipped subscriptions
covers: Expected: webhooks registered for OrderShipped behave exactly as today
items.reason: The ticket requires `OrderShipped` webhooks to behave exactly as today. Like TC-BUG-53-05, this pins the routing of an untouched sibling handler: subscriptions of type `OrderShipped`, `WebhookData.Type` `OrderShipped`, the event as payload. Shipping an order on the stack needs an admin flow outside this story, so the check runs in process in `tests/Application.UnitTests` with NSubstitute substitutes.

subject: BUG-53
reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): not passed; opus 9/10, sol 9/10; 1 finding(s) stand, 2 note(s).

items.reason: Both cases change the same seeded item's price and verify exactly one received message with its id and old/new prices. Combine them into the mixed-subscription case, retaining TC-BUG-53-01's registration-listing assertion and explicit initial-price check.

Story step 2 registers the webhook with 'the client's token'. TC-01/03/04 use their own tokens (bug53-price, bug53-same, bug53-mix-*). That only works because the stack leaves the webhooks client's ValidateToken unset (WebhookEndpoints.cs:13, the stack compose sets no ValidateToken). Add it as a precondition, or use the client's token and tell rows apart by arrival time.

'If the grid holds no rows at all, the None yet received placeholder is shown' is conditional on rows left by other cases in the in-memory HooksRepository, so it sometimes asserts nothing. Drop it or make it unconditional; the 'no row with token bug53-same' check is the real assertion.

items.reason: Tokens bug53-price/bug53-paid/bug53-shipped (and bug53-same in TC-BUG-53-03) are fixed literals, yet _index.md says the webhooks client's in-memory HooksRepository may survive a scenario reload. A second run against the same stack leaves a stale bug53-price row, so 'exactly one row' fails. The precondition 'no received message carrying them exists' says what must hold but not how. The cases should build each token from its prefix plus a per-run suffix (e.g. bug53-price-<runId>) and match the grid on the full value.
